Tips for Alice (Puppeteer, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so state your vote before each nomination and trial, then vote that way. If you switch, say why before the vote, because announced totals expose hidden mismatches. (seen in 30 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one mechanical case: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a broken claim, group elimination, or a lone visitor to a Katana victim. First ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester or Executioner). (seen in 32 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim, with no harmless explanation, is near-proof; don't let caveats acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat, and a role-block explains any missing result. 'Roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not support for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, but post results publicly by day. Deaths reveal no role, and the result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Repeated evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Budget is limited: ask a concrete question once, by name, and save budget for trials and the late rounds. (seen in 8 games)

## Village
- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 20 games)
- Stay quiet about power roles on Day 1. Don't be the loudest organizer, who is a common first Katana target. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is shown to be Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who pushed No or delay at the nomination, or defended them. Compare stated votes with the totals to find hidden votes. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link is a lead, never a hang on its own. Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. (seen in 28 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises, such as a slip naming a Yakuza-only role, far above awkward wording. (seen in 20 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool all game. Read every cause of death, press anyone who admits an action without naming it, and expect a multi-death ignite night. (seen in 17 games)
- Surviving a Katana attack proves nothing without a credible Medic: Neutrals have innate Defense. 'I was blocked' is unverifiable, but it fully explains a missing result. (seen in 15 games)
- Leave a likely Jester alive. If you must hang one, agree publicly on a bare Guilty majority, with confirmed power roles voting Innocent, since revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census. Use slot math to choose whom to press, audit or watch, then hang on the contradiction that test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually save them; do that math in night chat. On a likely-Jester nominee, some of you should vote Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Never put plans in daytime PMs. Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and the town treats a visible teammate PM cluster as a lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Fake claims must survive the real holder's counterclaim, token audits, exact-role checks and visit logs. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a hedge. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night: with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 21 games)
- After a failed attack, remove or block the protector instead of retrying. Kill Fortune Tellers and other info roles before their results build a shortlist. (seen in 19 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit the visit at once with it. (seen in 15 games)
- Use rig, puppet and other one-shot tokens early. Never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 18 games)
- Never speak from night-chat knowledge, e.g. who held the Katana or who was blocked. Village: demand the source of any such slip immediately. (seen in 7 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and never switch under pressure. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so say so when you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Fortune Teller
- Post both raw totals labeled by night every Day from Day 2, kept separate from your deductions. A visitor total of 1 on a Katana night makes the lone visitor the holder. (seen in 8 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators, rotating so a Pharmacist can't predict you. Spend a token on self-protection the night you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Dying with unused tokens is the usual failure. Set a trigger by Day 2-3, fire a 1-token Basic shot on a solid lead, and post it if the shot fails against innate Defense. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a Village player can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, and decide the night you can use it. Clerks who hold the token usually die with it. (seen in 18 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or 2 if anyone questions you. Douse players unlikely to be hanged soon. (seen in 12 games)

Tips for Frank (Ritualist, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so state your vote before each nomination and trial, then vote that way. If you switch, say why before the vote, because announced totals expose hidden mismatches. (seen in 30 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one mechanical case: an Evil result against a Vanilla claim, a broken claim, group elimination, or a lone visitor to a Katana victim. First ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester or Executioner). (seen in 32 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But a corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim, with no harmless explanation, is near-proof; don't let caveats acquit them. (seen in 29 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, roles can repeat, and a role-block explains any missing result. 'Roles can repeat' only means a claim isn't disproved; it is not support for it. (seen in 28 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, but post results publicly by day. Deaths reveal no role, and the result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 27 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked. Repeated evasion becomes its own case. (seen in 7 games)
- Budget is limited: ask a concrete question once, by name, and save budget for trials and the late rounds. (seen in 8 games)

## Village
- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 20 games)
- Stay quiet about power roles on Day 1. Don't be the loudest organizer, who is a common first Katana target. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is shown to be Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who pushed No or delay at the nomination, or defended them. Compare stated votes with the totals to find hidden votes. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link is a lead, never a hang on its own. Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. (seen in 28 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises, such as a slip naming a Yakuza-only role, far above awkward wording. (seen in 20 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool all game. Read every cause of death, press anyone who admits an action without naming it, and expect a multi-death ignite night. (seen in 17 games)
- Surviving a Katana attack proves nothing without a credible Medic: Neutrals have innate Defense. 'I was blocked' is unverifiable, but it fully explains a missing result. (seen in 15 games)
- Leave a likely Jester alive. If you must hang one, agree publicly on a bare Guilty majority, with confirmed power roles voting Innocent, since revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census. Use slot math to choose whom to press, audit or watch, then hang on the contradiction that test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually save them; do that math in night chat. On a likely-Jester nominee, some of you should vote Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Never put plans in daytime PMs. Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and the town treats a visible teammate PM cluster as a lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Fake claims must survive the real holder's counterclaim, token audits, exact-role checks and visit logs. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a hedge. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night: with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 21 games)
- After a failed attack, remove or block the protector instead of retrying. Kill Fortune Tellers and other info roles before their results build a shortlist. (seen in 19 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit the visit at once with it. (seen in 15 games)
- Use rig, puppet and other one-shot tokens early. Never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 18 games)
- Never speak from night-chat knowledge, e.g. who held the Katana or who was blocked. Village: demand the source of any such slip immediately. (seen in 7 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and never switch under pressure. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so say so when you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Fortune Teller
- Post both raw totals labeled by night every Day from Day 2, kept separate from your deductions. A visitor total of 1 on a Katana night makes the lone visitor the holder. (seen in 8 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators, rotating so a Pharmacist can't predict you. Spend a token on self-protection the night you claim. (seen in 21 games)

- Dying with unused tokens is the usual failure. Set a trigger by Day 2-3, fire a 1-token Basic shot on a solid lead, and post it if the shot fails against innate Defense. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a Village player can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, and decide the night you can use it. Clerks who hold the token usually die with it. (seen in 18 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or 2 if anyone questions you. Douse players unlikely to be hanged soon. (seen in 12 games)

- Post your role, night, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. If someone copies your claim, counterclaim at once with your full log. (seen in 16 games)
- Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM: it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 20 games)
- Stay quiet about power roles on Day 1. Don't be the loudest organizer, who is a common first Katana target. (seen in 24 games)
- Once a player is shown to be Yakuza by a mechanical result, suspect those who pushed No or delay at the nomination, or defended them. Compare stated votes with the totals to find hidden votes. (seen in 27 games)
- A PM link is a lead, never a hang on its own. Jesters and Executioners leave PM trails on purpose. (seen in 28 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises, such as a slip naming a Yakuza-only role, far above awkward wording. (seen in 20 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool all game. Read every cause of death, press anyone who admits an action without naming it, and expect a multi-death ignite night. (seen in 17 games)
- Surviving a Katana attack proves nothing without a credible Medic: Neutrals have innate Defense. 'I was blocked' is unverifiable, but it fully explains a missing result. (seen in 15 games)
- Leave a likely Jester alive. If you must hang one, agree publicly on a bare Guilty majority, with confirmed power roles voting Innocent, since revenge Divine-attacks a random Guilty voter. (seen in 15 games)
- An archive is a sample, not a census. Use slot math to choose whom to press, audit or watch, then hang on the contradiction that test produces. (seen in 14 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate unless the team's votes can actually save them; do that math in night chat. On a likely-Jester nominee, some of you should vote Innocent to stay out of the revenge draw. (seen in 34 games)
- Never put plans in daytime PMs. Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and the town treats a visible teammate PM cluster as a lead. (seen in 30 games)
- Fake claims must survive the real holder's counterclaim, token audits, exact-role checks and visit logs. Never claim a Yakuza-only role, even as a hedge. (seen in 18 games)
- Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night: with two Yakuza, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 19 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 21 games)
- After a failed attack, remove or block the protector instead of retrying. Kill Fortune Tellers and other info roles before their results build a shortlist. (seen in 19 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit someone could have seen. Agree a cover action in night chat and admit the visit at once with it. (seen in 15 games)
- Use rig, puppet and other one-shot tokens early. Never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 18 games)
- Never speak from night-chat knowledge, e.g. who held the Katana or who was blocked. Village: demand the source of any such slip immediately. (seen in 7 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and never switch under pressure. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, and a lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so say so when you post a Not Evil result. (seen in 16 games)

## Fortune Teller
- Post both raw totals labeled by night every Day from Day 2, kept separate from your deductions. A visitor total of 1 on a Katana night makes the lone visitor the holder. (seen in 8 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana: use it nightly on claimed investigators, rotating so a Pharmacist can't predict you. Spend a token on self-protection the night you claim. (seen in 21 games)

## Vigilante
- Dying with unused tokens is the usual failure. Set a trigger by Day 2-3, fire a 1-token Basic shot on a solid lead, and post it if the shot fails against innate Defense. (seen in 11 games)

## Clerk
- Rig a Day when a Village player can win a nomination but not a Guilty majority, and decide the night you can use it. Clerks who hold the token usually die with it. (seen in 18 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused, or 2 if anyone questions you. Douse players unlikely to be hanged soon. (seen in 12 games)

Task prompt
It is Day 2, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 6, 2.50x; next round 3.00x):
   10 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
   25 words: public 3.58, private 0.90
   50 words: public 4.74, private 1.18
  100 words: public 7.29, private 1.82
  200 words: public 13.33, private 3.33
  400 words: public 29.17, private 7.29
  800 words: public 75.83, private 18.96
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; leave it "" to keep it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; leave it "" to keep it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 2.50 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

R10 implies yes (everyone alive when the night began), so I delivered them, but neither role's text says so. 3) Phase labels: the log calls Night 1 '[Day 1 night]' and Night 2 '[Day 2 night]', while the rules number nights separately and say there is no Day 1. Results said 'Night 2' under a 'Day 2 night' header, which is easy to misread as off by one. 4) Seat order is never stated outright. I had to reconstruct the circle (Heidi, Judy, Mallory, Niaj, Alice, Bob, Carol, Dave, Erin, Frank, Grace, Ivan) from Day 2's speaking order to resolve Surveyor neighbors.",
 "missing_information": "I had no computed visit graph per night. I built the Cartographer and Scout groups by hand from each action and its type: visit, Astral (Oracle, Coroner, Cartographer map) or non-visit (Seer random pair). Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewThe Village won 9-3 without losing a player to a mis-hang. Every Yakuza was hanged on a chain of mechanical results. The decisive information came from three sources: - **Dave's Night 2 Cartographer sizes (3,2,2,1...).** Once Bob's, Mallory's and Grace's visits were placed, Heidi's killer had to be her lone 2-group partner. - **Niaj's Seer pairs.** Alice and Frank matched on Night 2, and Carol and Alice differed on Night 3. Carol was anchored as Good by Bob's Sheriff read and by her correct Oracle guesses. - **Ivan's Coroner exams.** These confirmed Alice as Puppeteer and Frank as Ritualist after each was hanged. Mallory's free Standard protection on the confirmed Seer stopped the Night 4 Katana, which bought a full extra cycle. The Yakuza lost mainly through passivity and avoidable tells: - They ended the game with every token unspent: the puppet token, both swap tokens and both ritual tokens. Frank even declined a near-certain Divine Ritualist guess of Seer on Niaj, who had been publicly confirmed. - Judy held the Katana all game and flatly denied visiting Heidi, while a Cartographer had already isolated Heidi's partner. - Alice sent Judy a visible Day 3 PM that was later cited against both of them. - Frank and Judy voted No/Innocent on each doomed teammate; the hidden vote logs show those Yakuza No votes making up the full No column on both Alice's and Frank's nominations. Village mistakes: - Dave fumbled his group arithmetic several times, which let the Yakuza attack his credibility. - Mallory never used her tokens to protect herself and died with 2 left. - Niaj misread his Night 5 Erin/Judy 'same' result as 'both Yakuza', when it actually reflected Judy holding the Katana and reading Good. Erin's elimination reasoning was the correct reading.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, prompt problemIn post-game feedback Mallory (Medic) said the token-cost line in her prompt seemed to contradict the rules, under which Standard protection is free and a token buys Strong. She had to infer that free Standard protection was allowed. The role prompt or summary for the Medic may misstate token costs.
Review: low, prompt problemThe Surveyor result text ('One of them, chosen at random, has the role Sheriff') was flagged by Grace as ambiguous about whether other group members could share the role. Grace then told the table 'exactly one of them is Sheriff/Oracle/Medic', which the result does not show. Clearer wording would prevent this misreading.
Review: low, player confusionOn Night 4 the Yakuza (Frank and Judy) turned down a Divine Ritualist guess on Niaj. Frank said a correct guess 'tells the victim I'm the Ritualist', and Judy said a Ritualist death 'exposes Frank'. Under R3/R12 a successful Ritualist kill reveals only the cause of death, not who the Ritualist is. Only a wrong guess publicly names the Ritualist. They misunderstood which outcome exposes the player.
Review: low, player confusionOn Day 3 Dave (Cartographer) wrongly said Heidi's Katana visit would be in the 3-group. He then gave several conflicting candidate lists, some leaving himself out and some including Frank. Other players treated the size-only output as if it named group members. Many later arguments said things like 'Dave's N2 sizes put Frank in a singleton', but sizes alone can't place a specific player. The Cartographer output (sizes only, no names without a map) confused several players.
Review: low, harness bugAn API retry error (HTTP 429 from OpenRouter, model anthropic/claude-opus-5.5) appeared in the game log during Night 5. It was retried and resolution went on correctly. It is a transient infrastructure error, not a game-logic problem.
